neo7.dev is a working notebook: engineering notes, tooling write-ups, and the details that only surface once something has actually been run.
The bias here is toward the specific. A note exists because working something out took longer than it should have, and writing it down is cheaper than working it out again.

data.what-does-not-go-here#What does not go h:
Anything written to look authoritative rather than to be useful. No tutorials reassembled from other people’s tutorials, and no commands that have not been run on a real machine.
Note Pages say so when they have not been re-tested against a current release. Confidence is cheap; a date and a version are not.
data.what-goes-here#What goes here:
Two kinds of thing, kept apart on purpose:
Docs are reference. They stay true, get looked up again, and only appear once a setup has been run end to end. Posts are time-bound. Something broke, something got decided, something took an afternoon that should have taken ten minutes. The split matters because the two age differently. A doc that drifts out of date is a bug; a post that is two years old is just a post from two years ago.

data.how-pages-are-written#How pages are writ:
Each page assumes you came for one answer and wants to get out of your way. Commands are the ones that were actually run, with the paths left real enough to be useful and nothing invented to fill a gap.
Where a page has not been re-tested against a current release, it says so. An untested page that looks confident is worse than no page.

data.what-this-section-is-for#What this secti:
Docs here are reference: things that stay true and get looked up again. A page earns a spot once its setup has been run start to finish and survived a reboot.
Anything time-bound — a debugging session, a decision and why it was made, a thing that broke — belongs in the blog instead.
